A.comparison: The 5.54 sentiment ratio versus the defined 0.58 corpus baseline recomputes to 9.55×, with the lane limitation stated.
A.chart: The monthly volume chart traces to c1 and has a unit, window, and claim, but does not chart the available critical or sentiment series and does not visibly mark censoring.
A.drilldown: Provides traced theme, entity, and geography layers plus specific follow-up questions; only three of six calls executed successfully, and no item-level headline layer is available.
A.export: Both needed summary and monthly tables are referenced and trace; provenance is present, but export hygiene falls short of the complete documented provenance shape and full capture details.
A.repro: Nearly all numbers trace and the call and window are listed; 28 of 29 traced prevents full reproducibility credit.

A.limits: Specific window, censoring, mention mode, lane, and geography caveats are placed near the claims; not every applicable coverage and pipeline limit is carried through.

A: The coverage series is topic mention matching and cannot establish lawsuit counts; the verdict correctly states this limitation.
B: Calling the February cluster mostly off-topic syndicated material is an interpretation, not a database finding; the deliverable labels it as interpretation.
The supplied source record does not establish that the recent compliance article was positive-polarity.
C: The 50–60 case count, cumulative series, and case-specific settlement and ruling details are memory estimates, not verified coverage measurements.
D: Claims that no dataset was supplied and that browsing was prohibited contradict the prompt.

raw.verdict: B is the strongest decision aid: it quantifies the news trend, exposes the anomalous February spike, and separates topic mentions from actual lawsuit counts. A is also careful about that core limitation, but B better uses the critical-series decomposition and covers more of the available facets.
